scope: Greater-metro outer belt & day-trip ring (Thu Duc/D9, D7/Phu My Hung, Tan Binh/airport, Bien Hoa-Dong Nai, Binh Duong, and the Cu Chi/Can Gio/Mekong/Tay Ninh/Vung Tau/Can Tho ring)

sights.address: 120 Hanoi Highway, Tan Phu Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The world's first Buddhism-themed amusement/water park (opened 1995), a surreal 200-ha spread of giant dragons, a neon-haloed Buddha shrine, a 'Buddhist Hell' walkthrough and waterslides pouring from sages' beards. ~1.5-2M visitors/year; daily ~07:30-17:00. Reachable on Metro Line 1.

sights.n: Vietnam National Historical Culture Park (Cong vien Lich su Van hoa Dan toc)
sights.address: Long Binh Ward, Thu Duc (District 9), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A ~400-ha state park recreating Vietnam's history in themed zones, anchored by the grand Hung Kings temple complex where the city holds its official Hung Kings' Death Anniversary rites. Long-running build-out; the ancient/Hung-Kings zone is the finished, visit-worthy core.

sights.n: Crescent Mall & Starlight Bridge (Cau Anh Sao)
sights.address: Ton Dat Tien, Phu My Hung, District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The centrepiece of planned Phu My Hung: a 170 m LED-lit pedestrian bridge over crescent-shaped Ho Ban Nguyet lake, glowing like a starry sky at night, beside the riverfront Crescent Mall. The go-to evening promenade of Saigon's affluent south.

sights.address: Hoang Van Thu, Tan Binh District (by Tan Son Nhat Airport), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A triangular 10.6-ha green lung immediately south of Tan Son Nhat airport, ringed by three boulevards, with lakes, shaded paths and a children's playground; open 24/7, free. The most convenient park for a stopover near the airport.

sights.address: Huynh Van Nghe, Buu Long Ward, Bien Hoa, Dong Nai, Vietnam
sights.w: An 84-ha scenic park nicknamed the 'Ha Long Bay of the South' for the limestone crags rising from emerald Long An lake (a flooded quarry), with boating, gardens and hilltop pagodas. ~30 km from central HCMC; open ~07:00-17:00 (closed Tuesdays).

sights.n: Cu Lao Pho & That Phu Ancient Temple (Ong Pagoda)
sights.address: Hiep Hoa (Cu Lao Pho), Bien Hoa, Dong Nai, Vietnam
sights.w: A Dong Nai river island that was the South's busiest trading port in the 1700s, founded by Chinese refugee Tran Thuong Xuyen; today a cluster of national-relic shrines, led by That Phu Ancient Temple (c.1684, the earliest Chinese temple in southern Vietnam) and Dai Giac Pagoda.

sights.address: Vinh Cuu District, Tri An, Dong Nai, Vietnam
sights.w: Vietnam's largest man-made reservoir (behind the Tri An hydro dam), a vast expanse dotted with ~76 forested islets, popular for boat trips, sunrise/sunset floats, island picnics and overnight fishing with local boatmen. ~65-70 km northeast of HCMC.

sights.n: Dai Nam Wonderland (Dai Nam Van Hien)
sights.address: Dai Nam, Thu Dau Mot, Binh Duong, Vietnam
sights.w: Vietnam's largest tourist complex (711 ha, opened 2008): an amusement park, a man-made 'sea' with wave beach, a zoo/safari, a racecourse and the colossal gilded Kim Dien (Dai Nam) temple, once the country's biggest. ~40 km north of HCMC.

sights.address: 4 Nguyen Du, Phu Cuong Ward, Thu Dau Mot, Binh Duong, Vietnam
sights.w: The Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) community's Mazu temple in Thu Dau Mot and the heart of the Chua Ba Festival on the 15th of the first lunar month, when a palanquin procession with 30+ lion-dance troupes draws hundreds of thousands through the town.

sights.address: Lai Thieu, Thuan An, Binh Duong, Vietnam
sights.w: A ~1,200-ha belt of riverside garden orchards famed for mangosteen and durian, where farms run agritourism visits, canal boat rides and fruit buffets in hammock-slung gardens. Season peaks May-August; the classic Saigon weekend fruit-picking escape.

sights.n: Ben Duoc Memorial Temple (Den Ben Duoc)
sights.address: Phu My Hung Commune, Cu Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A solemn state memorial temple at the far end of the Cu Chi tunnel zone, inscribed with the names of ~45,000 martyrs of the Saigon-Gia Dinh region; a 7-ha compound of carved murals and a nine-storey tower. The reflective counterpart to the tunnels' war-tourism.

sights.address: Ly Nhon Commune, Can Gio, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A ticketed eco-centre deep in the UNESCO Can Gio mangrove biosphere and a designated Ramsar site: a stork/heron bird sanctuary, a bat lagoon, a crocodile swamp and a watchtower over the wetlands. Distinct from the Monkey Island site, and the birders' pick.

sights.address: 1A Tran Phu (Nui Lon), Vung Tau, Vietnam
sights.w: A 100-ha mountaintop leisure park on Nui Lon reached by cable car, with a summit lake, gardens, a nightly musical-fountain 'Grand Show' and sweeping panoramas over Vung Tau and the sea.

sights.address: Hai Dang, Ward 2 (Nui Nho), Vung Tau, Vietnam
sights.w: Built by the French in 1862, the oldest of Vietnam's ~79 lighthouses, perched atop Nui Nho (Small Mountain); a short climb up 55 steps delivers a 360-degree view over the city, harbour and the Christ statue on the opposite hill.

sights.address: Thuy Van, Bai Sau, Vung Tau, Vietnam
sights.w: Vung Tau's main swimming beach, a ~10 km southeast-facing strand lined with loungers, seafood shacks and water sports (surf, SUP, kite-surf); the Saigonese weekend seaside default, two hours from the city.

sights.address: Hai Ba Trung, Ninh Kieu, Can Tho, Vietnam
sights.w: The riverfront symbol of Can Tho: a promenade park on the Hau River (named 1958) with a Ho Chi Minh statue, the Can Tho cable-stayed bridge views, the arched Ninh Kieu pedestrian bridge and an adjacent night market; the launch point for Cai Rang floating-market boats.

sights.address: Nguyen Trung Truc, My Phong, My Tho, Tien Giang, Vietnam
sights.w: The largest and most famous pagoda in Tien Giang (completed 1850), a national heritage site blending Vietnamese, Khmer, Chinese and European arches, set in gardens with giant Buddha statues; the standout stop on any My Tho / Mekong day trip.
